class.name: Feedback
class.brief_description: Players' feedback to the game's developer, through the online services.
class.description: A player's few words to you, sent from the game to your online services instance with what the game runs on: a bug they hit, an idea, a request for help. Give each kind its own category: [codeblock] var sent = await Feedback.send("bugs", text_edit.text, true) if not sent.ok: show_message("Couldn't send that. Try again later.") [/codeblock] Feedback is anonymous: nothing says who sent it, and email and IP addresses are removed from it. For a category where you'll want to answer (help with a purchase, say), turn on [code]feedback/<category>/named[/code] in Project Settings: that category's feedback names the player's account and display name, and keeps their words as written. Tell players which is which. You read it with [code]npm run feedback[/code] on your instance, or in a daily email. It's kept for 90 days.

method.name: is_available
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the player is signed in to the online services, so feedback can be sent.

method.name: send
method.description: Sends the player's [param text], 1 to 2000 characters, in [param category] (1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, [code]-[/code] or [code]_[/code]). It goes with the game's and engine's versions, the operating system, processor, memory and graphics card, and the context set with [method CrashReports.set_context]. With [param include_log], the last lines of this run's log go too, when file logging is on. Await it: the result has [code]ok[/code], and on failure [code]error[/code] and [code]message[/code] ([code]not_signed_in[/code], [code]bad_request[/code], [code]rate_limited[/code] after a few a minute, or [code]feedback_full[/code] once the game has had all it takes in a day).
